subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs OtherVendor (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs OtherVendor (Acme)

Hi Sam,

Great to connect earlier. Below is a short recap of our discovery, confirmed decision criteria, and the proposed bake-off plan. Please review and call out anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Highly variable inference spend during peak windows (month-end reports + field-assist spikes).
- Noticeable latency tail impacting field UX in locations with poor connectivity.
- Requirement for strict data isolation and auditability for QA/reg teams.

Stated business goals:
- Achieve >=30% reduction in per-token inference cost vs current baseline.
- Target sub-250ms 95th-percentile latency for responses under 1k tokens in US regions.
- Maintain audit log retention for at least 12 months to satisfy compliance.

Decision criteria we agreed on:
1) Performance & tail stability (95th pctl)
2) Cost predictability and recommendations for batching/quantization
3) Security/compliance (SOC2 Type II evidence, KMS support, private deployment option)
4) Operational tooling (trace-to-request, rollout controls)
5) Enterprise support and SLA commitments

Competitive notes:
- You mentioned OtherVendor’s trial shows good median latency but they lack persistent prefix/KV caching which increased cost in your sims.
- Redwood differentiators for this bake-off: unified routing (hosted/dedicated/private), explicit quantization profiles for accuracy/cost tradeoffs, and KV/prefix caching to reduce compute for repeated prefixes.

Proposed bake-off scope (high level):
- Window: Mar 9–13 (fixed prompt set).
- Tests: cold-start latency, 95th pctl under synthetic bursts, cost projection using production traces, and regression/accuracy on a 120-prompt set.
- Success: sub-250ms 95th pctl, >=30% monthly cost reduction projection, <2% accuracy regression vs baseline.

Next steps / action items:
- I attached the comparison sheet and a starter test plan.
- Please confirm evaluation owners and the anonymized data slice to use.
- If agreed, I’ll schedule a 45-minute kickoff on Mon Mar 9 to align the harness and provide Redwood trial access.

Attachments: redwood-vs-othervendor-compare.xlsx, acme-bakeoff-test-plan.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenna Morris <jenna.morris@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs OtherVendor (Acme)

Marissa,

Thanks for this — very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Internal owners: Jenna (product lead) and I will manage the business scoring; Rahul (DevOps) will run the performance harness. I will loop Rahul into the kickoff once we finalize timing.
- Data: we’ll use anonymized field-assist traces from the March run (~30k requests).
- OtherVendor note: they don’t support persistent KV caching which increased simulated cost by ~20% in our runs. If Redwood’s KV/prefix caching behaves as described that’s likely a key differentiator.

I attached an updated test plan with slight timing/load edits. Can Redwood confirm ability to sustain the synthetic burst (3x baseline for 3 minutes) and share recommended batching windows to balance cost/latency?

Also: we require SOC2 Type II evidence and a KMS integration plan before moving any sensitive data into trial systems. Could you share the redacted SOC2 and a KMS checklist?

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Director, Product | Acme Manufacturing
sam.patel@acme.com
Attachment: acme-bakeoff-test-plan-updated.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs OtherVendor (Acme)

Hi Sam,

Thanks — good notes. Quick confirmations:
- Participants: please loop Rahul into the kickoff and I’ll add Michael (solutions lead) to own trial config and quantization.
- Burst capability: Redwood can sustain the 3x burst for short windows and we’ll provide a recommended batching window (our initial suggestion: 25–50ms for your request mix). We’ll validate after the first run and adjust.
- SOC2 & KMS: attaching our control mapping and redacted SOC2 report; see one-page KMS checklist (options: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer-managed HSM).

Proposed kickoff: Mon Mar 9 @ 10:00 AM PT — 45 minutes to align harness, provide temporary access keys, and confirm scoring scripts. Does that work for you and Rahul?

What I’ll do now:
1) Share trial endpoints and temporary API keys via secure link.
2) Populate recommended config and quantization profile in the comparison sheet.
3) Prepare a short runbook for test execution and scoring.

Links/attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3D4efGHIJklmN (SOC2 redacted & control mapping), redwood-vs-othervendor-compare.xlsx

Best,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap — Redwood vs OtherVendor (Acme)

Hi Sam — quick technical note before kickoff:

- We’ll provide a small harness (Docker image + test runner) to replay your anonymized traces against Redwood and OtherVendor endpoints. The harness will record latency distributions and token counts so you have apples-to-apples cost projections.
- For the synthetic burst we recommend two variants: 1) burst-only (3x for 3 minutes), and 2) burst-plus-sustained (3x burst then 1.5x sustained for 30 minutes) to evaluate tail under mixed traffic.
- We’ll expose temporary read-only access to request logs (no raw PII) and full audit logs in the control plane for the retention window you require.

I’ll drop the Docker image and README in the shared Drive folder by EOD today. If you have test scripts you prefer, we can integrate them.

See you on Mar 9 — I’ll join the kickoff and walk through the harness.

—Dev
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
